items.summary: Join the show for more Elden Ring.
items.content:
Video ShackStream: Elden Ring on The Stevetendo Show! Episode 749 Join the show for more Elden Ring.

Tonight, on The Stevetendo Show, we’re jumping right back into our Elden Ring playthrough. I have limited experience with these types of games, having played Dark Souls 1 on The Stevetendo Show and a cup of coffee in Dark Souls 3. During the last Elden Ring episode, we started our journey, and it went about as well as you would have expected.

We died quite a few times, but I was teaching myself the basics of the game. We started the episode Torent-less and maiden-less. By the time we finished, we had both of those things and killed a cave-dwelling boss. Will I be able to make my way through the game, dealing with all the enemies I come across? Set to go live at 5 p.m. PT/8 p.m. ET, join The Stevetendo Show for more of our Elden Ring playthrough.

Shackers who want to join in on the fun can head over to the Shacknews Twitch channel, where you can tune into The Stevetendo Show every Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.

If you can't make tonight's show, you can watch Monday nights at 6 p.m. PT/9 p.m. ET. Coming up on the show are more of our Pokemon XD: Gale of Darkness and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time playthroughs. The schedule could look a little different in the near future with the likes of Super Mario Sunshine and Star Fox Adventures coming on the scene. The action is heating up, and you won't want to miss out!

Be sure to check out the Shacknews Twitch channel and the Shacknews VODs YouTube channel. Catch up on some of your favorite Shacknews programs with a subscription to the YouTube channel and a follow to the Twitch channel. If you aren’t aware, Shacknews has a new service for you called Shackmaps . The lovely Shacknews staff has gone through some of your favorite video games to keep you from getting lost. There are new maps coming soon, so sign up now!

With all the technical issues we had last night, I didn't get to share my thoughts on the Legend of Zelda fortieth anniversary Direct. I'll kill two birds with one stone this evening because I'll share my thoughts on the Nintendo Direct that occurred this morning. It was an interesting presentation that had a few games that caught my attention. Swing by the show to hear my thoughts!

Re-reading what I wrote yesterday, none of the games I predicted were shown during the Direct presentation. No Rad Racer, no Mario, no F-Zero. One of these days, we’ll get the classic Rad Racer on the Switch Online, but I guess we’ll have to settle for Star Fox Adventures. Keep thinking of games that you’d like me to play on The Stevetendo Show. If they’re easy to get ahold of/on Switch Online, you could see them star in an upcoming episode.

Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review – A Masterpiece in Your Hands
items.summary: The Elden Ring Tarnish Edition brings together the beloved ARPG and its excellent DLC as one package for the Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
Back when it was released in 2024, I gave Elden Ring a score of 98. Four years later, and considering I have well over 1000 hours of play time on PC and PS5, I still wonder if my score was too low. For me, Elden Ring is the absolute pinnacle of FromSoftware’s design philosophy and the gold standard for open world action games. It’s now hard to put myself in the shoes of someone playing Elden Ring for the first time. Considering that around 30-40% of Switch 2 owners don’t have a gaming PC or other high-end console, there’s a good chance that gamers picking up the Tarnished Edition will be dropping in for the first time. Lucky them.

The Tarnished Edition brings together the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, itself maybe the best DLC ever released for a game. It also includes a handful of new weapons, two new classes, and skins for Torrent, the player’s mount. These add-ons are also available for $4.99 for PC and console games who already own the game. Accessing the game’s co-op and PvP features means having a subscription to Nintendo Switch Online.

If you’ve already played Elden Ring on PC or another console, you’re probably just wondering how it fares on Nintendo Switch 2. Elden Ring on the go sounds like a dream come true. The good news is that it runs just fine, if you’re willing to accept some limitations. Frame rates are capped at 30fps. Textures and ray tracing are a little simplified and a bit blurry, especially in handheld mode. On the other hand, the beauty of Elden Ring is in its art, character and environmental designs. It doesn’t depend on photorealism. In combat, the 30fps throttle is a little more frustrating, and framerates dip a little in the more intense boss battles. Bottom line, the Switch 2 is powerful enough to run Elden Ring and players will have the full experience.

If you’ve never played a FromSoftware game, be prepared for some narrative confusion. The developer is known for stories that are opaque, dense with lore and full of sadness, darkness, and fading hope. With an assist by George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring’s narrative tells of a shattered world. The demigod children of Queen Marika have torn the realm apart. The player takes on the role of a Tarnished, tasked with slaying the corrupt demigods and claiming the title of Elden Lord.

It should be noted that with any FromSoft game, there are fans who dive deep into the lore. At the other end, there are even more players who simply ignore most of the narrative and focus on exploration and combat. Elden Ring rewards either approach. For anyone who’s confused, there’s an immense amount of material online about the characters and their complex relationships.

When it comes to action and combat, Elden Ring represents a major step forward and brings together mechanics explored in other games from the developer. There are few — if any — action RPGs with boss battles as finely tuned as those in Elden Ring. The number of weapons, armor sets, and ways to use magic is staggering in its variety. Like most RPGs, Elden Ring has starting classes but these are largely ignored by players past the first few hours. That said, the Tarnished Edition adds two extremely viable classes in the form of the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight.

Souls games have a well-earned reputation for difficulty, and FromSoftware has resisted adding difficulty options. That’s because they’re built in. Especially in Elden Ring, if players are struggling there are always areas to visit and lower level enemies to kill. There are other weapons or spells to try. The game’s system for summoning Spirit Ashes allows players to call on extremely competent AI companions to help out. Compared to exacting platformers where there is no margin for error, FromSoft’s games feel, if not forgiving, at least balanced and fair.

Outside of combat, exploration is extremely rewarding thanks to a fast travel system and Torrent, your mount. While Elden Ring’s map isn’t the biggest open world it feels immense due to layers of verticality and subterranean areas to explore. No area feels too empty and between the labyrinthine Legacy Dungeons and open landscapes, there’s always something to discover or fight. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC added a significant amount of new content to an already massive game.

If you haven’t played Elden Ring, and the Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 has enticed you, please make the leap. I envy you seeing it all for the first time. If you have the game on other consoles or PC and don’t own something like a Steam deck or ROG Ally, the Elden Ring you love is there and intact, but with the visual downgrade that you probably expect. In the end, more Elden Ring is a very good thing.

***Switch 2 code provided by the publisher for review***

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Tarnished Edition sounds about right to me.
items.content:
The Lands Between beckon again, and Nintendo finally gets a release of one of 2022s best games and this time, it includes the DLC Shadow of the Erdtree. Is it worth venturing into the world created by George R.R. Martin, or is it as disappointing as the final season of Game of Thrones? Elden Ring was a game I picked up on PC originally a little after it came out. I promptly played it for a handful of hours and quit. Partly because I was frustrated at the difficulty spikes, partly because something else neat and shiny came out right after I purchased it (Hogwarts Legacy, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, etc. take your pick.) This newly released Nintendo Switch 2 version gave me the chance to dive back in and see The Lands Between again.

The opening cinematic is nothing new for Elden Ring players and features the same scenes, script, etc. Tarnished Edition’s character creation has 2 new classes, the Idus Knight and the Heavy Knight. The Idus Knight starts with pretty good dexterity and strength scores and comes equipped with armor and weaponry that doesn’t slow you down. While the Heavy Knight, as the name suggests, is more of a beefy tank with very high strength stats right away with heavy armor and weaponry making dodges a little harder.

After the opening cinematic, and character creation, players are dropped into a small opening area that can’t be explored much. After about five to ten minutes of wandering around, your first enemy appears, and it’s a boss right away. Don’t worry about defeating it, I never came close to doing so. After the intro into how insane the difficulty is going to be later, players are dropped into a cave with two directions, go deeper into the cave, or leave. If you go deeper into the cave, it serves as the games tutorial and rewards you with a little bit of extra runes (the game’s money and experience).

Elden Ring’s combat is designed to be very precise. This requires players to stay on their toes and learn enemy patterns. Some enemies you can just walk right up to and hit, even in the middle of their animation. While you’re fighting in Elden Ring take care not to attract too much attention. Fighting one or two low level enemies is easy, but when you start getting a few more, (or an enemy that doesn’t flinch when you hit them along with a few wimps) it’s very easy to die. And die you will……. A lot.

Death, just like in other souls likes, makes you drop all your runes where you died. There is a compass at the top of the screen that helps guide you back to where you died to get your runes back. Be careful, if you die along the way your original drop disappears and is replaced by where you died…. Again.

“Sites of grace” are save points in the game that if you die, you will return to. Eventually, when you rest at a specific site of grace you meet an NPC named Melina, who offers you an accord. This allows you to spend runes to level up your character. When leveling up, pick a single stat and raise it by a point, each point you put into a stat costs an increasing amount of runes. Putting points into vitality increases your hit points while strength increases damage from melee weapons and increases your carry capacity.

Elden Ring is a game that wants you to explore. Don’t just go straight to a boss. That was my mistake the first time playing through. As you explore you gain runes, enemies drop better equipment. There are enemies called Teardrop Scarabs in the opening area that can drop more rare and valuable items, some will even upgrade your rechargeable healing flask.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version graphically isn’t as powerful as the PS5 or Xbox Series X. Is it worth revisiting Elden Ring again if you own this game on other platforms? In short, not really. After just an hour into this version I could already see that the Switch 2 wasn’t fully up to the task. While the game still looks good, there was plenty of slowdown in the open areas. In a game where survival depends so much on very well-timed attacks, and defense, seeing the game skip a few frames at inopportune times will kill the experience. It’s painfully obvious that the Switch 2 struggles to keep up. When compared to the PC version, even on an older gaming rig, I’d much rather play it on PC.

Don’t misunderstand, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is still a great game, warts and all. It is frustratingly hard, especially if you end up accidentally bypassing some opening areas and save points (like I did both times I played the opening area). If the Switch 2 is what you have, or want to play Elden Ring on the go, pick it up on Switch 2. But if you have something more powerful to play it on, I would recommend PC personally, but PS5 or Xbox Series X would work just as well.

Note: Bandai Namco provided us with a Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Switch 2 code for review purposes.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Switch 2 means you can now touch grace AND grass
Review: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition (Nintendo Switch 2)
items.content:
Elden Ring is an incredible game, and I already have a very in-depth review covering why I consider it to be a genuine masterpiece within the “games-as-art” canon. I’m not going to re-litigate that in reviewing the Switch 2 release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition. Everything that applied to that original review applies here as well. In fact, it’s genuinely impressive just how completely the gothic ambience translates to the Switch’s relatively humble screen.

Just to be up-front about this though: the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring is a slight downgrade from its big console and PC brothers. It’s truly impressive that the downgrade manifests itself in such minor ways, with loading times that are a second or two longer, or a framerate that is very steady, but not quite as silken. However, those compromises (particularly the frame rate) do matter for a game that is as demanding on timing and precision as Elden Ring is.

There’s also a small issue from the hardware itself. The Switch 2’s Joy-Cons don’t offer quite the same nuanced travel as a standard controller, so if you’re playing the game in handheld mode, you’ve got ever-so-slightly less depth of control. Again, it by no means makes Elden Ring unplayable, but, again, for a game as demanding on its players as Elden Ring, those tiny nuances will matter. The long and short of it is that if you’re playing Elden Ring on another platform, I’m not 100% sure you’ll be sold on grabbing it on Switch 2 as well. I, personally, much prefer the portability and am happy for the compromises for that form factor, but I also realise that I’m something of an outlier in that regard.

Mind you, none of what I said didn’t apply to the Nintendo Switch port of Dark Souls back in the day, and when I log into that game from time to time I still see the occasional ghostly outline wandering around. Clearly there is an audience for these things, and I don’t want to understate just how impressive it is that an open world as drenched in atmosphere and expansive in scope as Elden Ring is plays on the Switch 2. And you get the universally celebrated expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree, to go with the universally celebrated base game. The world looks utterly gorgeous on the Switch 2’s screen, and while I was initially concerned that the smaller form factor would make it harder to make out key details, I’ve had no issue whatsoever in making my way around the world again.

The only other downside that needs to be noted is the multiplayer. Perhaps because the frame rates between versions are slightly different (which would make things much tougher for a Switch 2 player), Elden Ring’s multiplayer isn’t cross-play. You can only team up with or go to war with other Switch 2 players. This is a bummer to people who might have wanted to buddy up with specific players on a different platform, but, again, I do have to note that Dark Souls had no issue with the multiplayer experience being populated on the Switch, and I cannot imagine that the long-term case will be any different for Elden Ring. This is one of those games that most people would feel an urge to own, so if you’re counting on getting some randoms into your game to help with one of the bosses, I would be surprised if you’re waiting for long.

This has been a difficult review to write. Firstly, because everything that makes Elden Ring a special experience is not exclusive to the Switch 2 release, I really recommend you read my review of the original game to get an understanding of just how strongly I feel about this game. Everything I wrote in that review applies here too. But also, in acknowledging that the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring isn’t quite up to the standard of the game playing on the PlayStation 5, this review sounds more negative than it should. The differences are a rounding error, and what is important is that this masterpiece runs perfectly well on a very portable console.

items.title: Game Review: Elden Ring – Tarnished Edition (Switch 2)
items.content:
Elden Ring is objectively one of the greatest games of all time. Few would disagree, even if the difficulty barrier and Fromsoftware storytelling kept them from exploring one of the most intriguing open worlds ever created. I played Elden Ring for 100 hours in 2022 on the PS5 at launch, therefore my time with the Switch 2 version was more about performance than the many breathtaking moments and discoveries in that original playthrough. Still, I did not review Elden Ring in 2022 for a very specific reason – my previous attempts at souls games ended with a level of frustration that did not transfer well to the review process. Elden Ring changed everything, becoming my gateway into the genre and one of the most refreshing open world experiences in some time. I have since reviewed and beaten countless soulslike games, understanding the genre and the ‘die to improve’ mantra. The Switch 2 version – Tarnished Edition – comes packed with all the extras (including the fantastic Shadow of the Erdtree DLC). It is full of more features than the original release, but the question on everyone’s mind is this – how does it perform on Nintendo’s latest console?

Before I answer the core question, it is best to set the scene for newcomers. Elden Ring is an action/adventure game set in the Lands Between. Your goal is to become the Elden Lord by repairing the Elden Ring, yet you are a maiden-less tarnished (a banished warrior). Your ancestors were stripped of the Erdtree’s guiding light, and the game ensures it is known that you are very much at the bottom of the barrel. To say more would include me mentioning names, relationships and age-old battles that are best discovered in-game. The narrative is a challenge to piece together – you’ll meet a random NPC, they’ll ask you to do something or tell you their tale, and then you’ll continue on without any markers or clue to how to help them. 20 hours later, something or someone triggers a memory of this chat and a thread may start to form. The overarching narrative of defeating demigods to become the Elden Lord is fairly clear, but all else is draped in shadow and it takes lengthy YouTube vids to decipher the tale. Still, the mystery is welcomed in a medium that is all too quick to tell us everything. A second playthrough removes many of the strengths as you know what’s around most corners, yet there is depth in builds that prolongs the experience.

When I play souls games, I generally go with the sword and board (shield) approach as magic and other more niche approaches require in-depth knowledge of builds. As you are gaining levels and needing to choose which of many attributes to increase, you really need a plan in how you want your character to play. Are they all out attack up close, are they causing bleed, are they shooting spells from distance? Choosing a build is your best way to master the challenges ahead, otherwise you are peppering the stats with a scattergun that only makes bosses harder. On this occasion, I went with a samurai that also dabbled in sorcery. The samurai class uses katanas, precision, bleed and positioning to succeed. By adding a staff in my second hand, I now had spells as a projectile rather than the bow (you can swap around with countless weapons, which is half the fun). This allowed my playthrough 4 years later to be distinct, engaging with features that I didn’t really bother with in 2022. It shows the depth involved, as the game is already a colossus in its best aspect: the open world.

As we know with open world games, they are only as good as their sense of exploration and discovery. If we know there’s a point of interest around the bend, is the journey as good as the destination? Rarely. Elden Ring is best in class as there are so many naturally found secrets across an ever-expanding world. Every player will tell you about the first time they discovered a certain lift down to another world, or when they stumbled out of one massive area only to see an equally massive area reveal itself upon a hill. Many aspects of the map will never be seen by players, which makes discovering them and exploring them rewarding – even if the loot found isn’t making you any more powerful. Finding a site of grace (save point and opportunity to enhance level) is the way to plot out the map, all the way to extremely difficult boss fights and dungeons. Finding a site of grace after half an hour of collecting and fighting brings a sense of relief almost unmatched in gaming. Enemy variety is strong despite some re-used mini-bosses, biomes are diverse and unique, and there are insane moments of lore despite not presenting in a traditional sense. All of this combines to create an open world experience for the ages.

Now, onto performance. I put equal time into docked and handheld on the Switch 2. While a game requiring precision movement and skill is better operated through a general controller, the handheld version here appeared to have better framerates and textures. Elden Ring was never a graphical masterpiece, instead thriving off brilliant art design and lighting. It is clear that the Switch 2 makes some sacrifices to see availability for such a demanding title, but the game plays and looks very good overall as a port. There is some slowdown during boss fights and the distances can pop in a little at times, but I was left impressed (especially handheld) on how well it ran overall. I found this to be stronger in presentation than Final Fantasy 7: Rebirth (the closest comparison in game world and action pace) which may in part be due to the darker tone. Either way, if you are a fan of the game or have always been intrigued this is a great purchase on the Switch 2.

Elden Ring is a juggernaut that will forever be reference in the greatest game of all time discussions. With a movie on the way, the IP will continue to be in the spotlight – now available for gamers on all systems. While Nintendo is not renowned for darker games, 2026 has provided excellent ports to bridge the gap for gamers keen to dabble in both first party and third party offerings. Never has there been a better time to journey through the Lands Between.

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

items.title: How to utterly embarrass yourself while "playing" Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike...
items.content:
Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike games are not my area of expertise. Regardless, the Nintendo Switch 2 port of Elden Ring and its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion – now bundled as the Tarnished Edition – remains one of the biggest third-party releases on the console this year, and I figured this would be a great opportunity to see if I was cut out for the challenge of one of 2022’s top-rated games.

Spoilers: I was not cut out for said challenge.

If you want to learn all about how to make an absolute fool of yourself while playing Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2, read on.

Elden Ring has a remarkably robust character creator that lets you adjust practically every pore of your warrior’s face. I can’t recall the last time I played a game in which I had so many distinct ways to negligibly adjust the size and positioning of a character’s nose and nostrils. And of course, all of this is a critical step towards getting immersed in the adventure to come.

I probably should have spent the same amount of time considering my character’s class. I opted to go into this game completely blind, so I just flipped through the list of classes and picked the one that seemed the most relevant to how I would normally play an action RPG, ultimately landing on the Bandit class. This seemed to be wise at the outset, because I figured that having a bow as well as a blade would be useful, probably leaving me well-equipped for most foes I would encounter in the early game.

While it wasn’t a horrible choice, I did find myself wishing pretty quickly that I had opted for a build with some more oomph. Having a knife that I could swing quickly felt good, as it allowed me to be nimble, but at least in the early game I didn’t get a ton of use out of having a bow on hand. Meanwhile, the character I made – a snow-haired stud I named Alabaster – spent 80% of his screen time with his face obscured by armor. Go figure. The good news is that, as the game progresses, there are plenty of ways to customize both your playstyle and your look, so you’re not locked into anything major.

How this version of Elden Ring might perform has been the subject of much conversation prior to launch. A world as sprawling and moody as The Lands Between is typically something I’d want to experience on the biggest screen possible. So it’s a real shame that I spent as much time fighting the game’s frame rate as I did fighting Godrick Knights – in docked mode, at least.

It’s not unplayable by any means, but it’s also far from perfect. Elden Ring’s docked frame rate heavily fluctuates depending on what is happening onscreen; generally it seemed like the more interesting the environment was, the more often I would encounter issues. There were times when it was so noticeable that it even made Alabaster’s running animation look a bit stilted. The game itself looks really good on the big screen – although not quite comparable to other platforms in terms of fine details – but given the scale of the world, the density of foliage and foes, and the very impressive lighting effects, it’s an understandable compromise.

In handheld mode, though, the game looks and runs immaculately. It’s a bewildering experience playing a game like this on such a slim device, and the fact that it looks as crisp and runs as smooth as it does in this mode is truly a miracle. I would also say that the smaller screen helps mask some of the DLSS and (what appears to be) dynamic resolution scaling better than while playing in docked mode.

I mean, sure, that giant tentacle monster slithering along the beach doesn’t look like a friendly fella, but it’s in the game’s opening section of the map. The developers wouldn’t seriously place such a high level foe right in the way of a player who is just trying to wander of the beaten path only a little, would they?

I know I shouldn’t be too surprised that Elden Ring doesn’t hesitate to destroy players who get a little too big for their britches, but it’s not just the big beasts that will KO you. Just about anything in this game can pose a serious threat if you are underleveled, underequipped, or underskilled as a player. I definitely felt like I fit into all three of those categories… well, the entire time I spent playing Elden Ring, really.

This game, in fact, does have quite a few similarities to Nintendo’s highly acclaimed Zelda adventure. Extremely sparse storytelling that’s mostly delivered as a by-product of exploration? Check. A cool horse? Check. Picking up resources to craft stuff and cook? Check. A wide open world that is so unfathomably massive that you wonder if you will ever possibly see everything in it? Check.

So, you’ll have to forgive my muscle memory as I repeatedly tried to climb things that could not be climbed (read: most things), jump over things that could not be jumped over, and casually wander into places that, apparently, are always filled with dangerous creatures that can wreck me in about 2 hits. In the opening area? And people play these games… for fun?!

Very early on in Elden Ring, I stumbled across a little camp of soldiers across from a huge castle gate. With my (theoretically) lighter and stealthier build, I figured I could probably just off them one by one without raising the alarm. I also figured there was probably some good stuff tucked away in there that would help me not be so much of a pushover.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: The Duskbloods isn't just 'Nintendo Bloodborne', it's better than Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: It doesn't deserve the hate it's been getting.
items.content:
The Duskbloods is a solid multiplayer experience and proof FromSoftware can do more than just traditional soulsborne.

FromSoftware’s Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods , recently finally invited players to see what it’s all about - and despite some initial technical hiccups, I actually quite enjoyed it.

Before I dive into my thoughts and feelings, I can confidently say that my time with The Duskbloods was more enjoyable than Elden Ring: Nightreign . That’s not to say I don’t like Nightreign , but aside from the odd game with friends, it never gave me much of a reason to stick around.

The Duskbloods felt different however. Once the server issues were mended and players could finally jump into some matches, it was clear this is more than FromSoftware trying to relive its Bloodborne glory days.

You’ll no doubt have seen some of the memes online, but when it came time to select a character, I felt compelled to choose Zork.

This goofy little guy perfectly exemplifies why The Duskbloods is a completely different animal to any other FromSoftware game.

Each character has their own unique design, fighting style, special abilities and general stat loadout. As a strength build aficionado, Zork looked like the right choice for me and boy oh boy was I correct.

Aside from his heavy weapon and bulky armour, Zork’s ability lets him ascend into the air and become a living missile directed at anything you’re locked on to.

I let out a hearty chuckle every time I chased down a fleeing player with this move, and even when I went off course and paid the price, it was still a good laugh. His other move is a missile barrage, which was great for pummelling enemies at range.

Once you’re accustomed to what your character can do, your objective is to kill. Like Elden Ring: Nightreign , slaying enemies gradually levels you up, but what I love about The Duskbloods is there’s no penalty for biting off more than you can chew. If you die, your level remains the same, meaning you can spawn back in and have another go, or wander off in search of easier prey.

Sigils are scattered throughout the map hiding powerful NPC allies, which you can summon like eldritch Pokémon to help you overpower foes, or just draw their attention while you heal up from afar. Again, this gave me a good laugh, especially one that sang opera before giving an unsuspected enemy the prime Hoarah Loux experience (just straight hands and elbow drops).

The ultimate goal is to raise your level as high as possible within the time-limit, as the players with the lowest rank get eliminated from the game.

Those fortunate or skilled enough to make it to the end take part in one final battle against your fellow survivors, for the ultimate glory.

In essence, that’s what I loved most about The Duskbloods, and it completely rid me of my woes over the game being PvPvE.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States
